events.title: Oil and security shocks in the second half of 2014
events.statement: The World Bank's Spring 2016 outlook describes simultaneous oil-price and ISIS-related shocks beginning in the second half of 2014.
events.source_locator: Opening discussion of the twin crisis
events.limit: This is the source's assessment of several overlapping developments, not a causal result produced by this program. The half-year boundaries are a display window, not exact shock dates.

events.title: Pandemic and oil-revenue shock in 2020
events.statement: The IMF's 2020 consultation, published in February 2021, describes pandemic pressures and a sharp decline in oil revenues during 2020.
events.source_title: Executive Board Concludes 2020 Article IV Consultation with Iraq
events.limit: The annual period contains several shocks. A February 2021 assessment must not be treated as information known throughout 2020.

events.title: Recovery and higher oil revenue in 2021
events.statement: The World Bank's Spring 2022 monitor describes a 2021 recovery with eased movement restrictions, changing oil-production conditions and higher oil revenue.
events.source_title: Iraq Economic Monitor, Spring 2022: Harnessing the Oil Windfall for Sustainable Growth
events.source_locator: Opening two paragraphs on the 2021 recovery
events.limit: Context for 2021, reported in 2022. Estimates and projections in the same report must retain their different status.

events.title: Fiscal expansion starting in 2023
events.statement: The IMF's 2024 consultation describes a large fiscal expansion starting in 2023 under Iraq's three-year budget.
events.limit: This entry refers to the year expansion began, not an exact budget-adoption date. Approved allocations must be distinguished from recorded execution.

events.title: New official dollar rates take effect
events.statement: The CBI announcement dated 7 February 2023 says the new rates apply from 8 February: 1300 IQD/USD for Ministry of Finance purchases, 1310 for platform sales to banks and 1320 for end users.
events.source_title: The Central Bank of Iraq begins selling dollars at the new official rate
events.limit: Different transaction rates are not interchangeable. This announcement supplies no continuous parallel-market series and does not establish the effect on any selected chart.

events.title: Unpaid obligations discussed for 2024
events.statement: The IMF's 2025 report discusses arrears accumulation in 2024 and financing and budget-execution constraints.
events.source_title: Iraq: 2025 Article IV Consultation, Country Report 25/183
events.source_locator: Paragraphs 7 and 19; printed pages 5 and 12 / PDF pages 10 and 17
events.limit: The source describes obligations and financing constraints. It does not identify theft. IMF definitions and estimates must not be silently substituted for CBI cash-account figures.

evidence.title: How researchers estimate hidden economic activity
evidence.statement: An IMF working paper compares survey and national-account approaches with indirect currency-demand and MIMIC methods for estimating the shadow economy.
evidence.limit: No numerical Iraq shadow-economy series has been validated or imported into this application. This reference explains methods; it is not a corruption detector or a monthly measure.

source.title: Shadow Economies Around the World: What Did We Learn Over the Last 20 Years?
source.locator: Section 3: estimation methods and their strengths and weaknesses

evidence.title: Jobs and economic production need different measurements
evidence.statement: The IMF's 2021 measurement paper proposes a framework for informal production that is consistent with national-account concepts.
evidence.limit: A measurement framework does not supply an Iraq monthly shadow-economy dataset. The existing app cannot derive hidden production from a budget residual.

evidence.title: Spending recorded in cash can miss unpaid obligations
evidence.statement: The IMF's 2025 report says Iraq accumulated substantial domestic arrears in 2024, including obligations for fuel, electricity and capital expenditure, amid financing constraints.
evidence.limit: This is a published assessment of 2024, not a finding produced from the selected chart. Different perimeters and accounting bases must remain separate. Arrears do not establish theft.

source.title: Iraq: 2025 Article IV Consultation, Country Report 25/183
source.locator: Paragraphs 7 and 19, printed pages 5 and 12 / PDF pages 10 and 17

evidence.title: A discrepancy is a question to check, not an audit finding
evidence.statement: The IMF report records authorities' discussion of stronger public-financial management, audits and enforcement. This app currently contains no individual audited loss or theft finding.
evidence.limit: The IMF passage is an account of authorities' views, not an individual audit finding. A residual can reflect timing, definitions, revisions, missing accounts or unpaid obligations. This application cannot identify theft or a recipient from aggregate accounts.

summary.target: Percentage change in WDI total real GDP (constant local currency), not GDP per person or fiscal revenue.
summary.specification: Growth(t) = intercept + previous GDP growth + previous price-adjusted spending growth proxy + previous world-oil-price growth.

next_year.interval: Conventional OLS conditional normal-error approximation; not calibrated probability or a policy effect.
next_year.latest_actual_status: Historical source values; may be estimates or revisions; not a real-time-vintage origin.
next_year.origin_role: Input reference year, not the date when all inputs became available
next_year.availability_note: Saved in October 2026 using later-released 2025 fiscal/GDP values. This prediction could not have been issued at 2025 year-end with these inputs.

evaluation.design: Fixed specification, expanding window, identical past-only one-year test targets; revised snapshot, not real-time-vintage evaluation.
evaluation.model_tuning: No tuning or model selection using held-out targets. Specification predeclared; next-year model is not chosen because it won the test.
evaluation.interval_coverage_limit: Very few targets; observed coverage cannot validate nominal calibration.

reasons: Only 18 complete level rows; project gate requires 40 annual rows for a two/three-variable VECM investigation.
Common valuation, coverage, price base, revisions and seasonal treatment need a documented review.
The fixed-lag ADF/KPSS screen does not consistently support all variables being I(1); tests need interpretation and break sensitivity.
Cointegration rank is absent, full, unavailable or sensitive to lag/deterministic assumptions.
vecm.decision_scope: This candidate failed the current data/specification checks. That is not a conclusion that a VECM is impossible for Iraq.

compatible_verified_series.variable: Total real GDP after imputed bank-service charges

remaining_gates: Review every candidate table and quarter mapping; reconcile reported overlaps using a documented common revision policy.
Confirm common GDP valuation, geographic coverage, 2007 price base, imputed services and seasonal treatment.
Align only complete quarterly spending flows and clearly defined oil inputs to that reviewed GDP series.
Then assess integration/rank/lag/deterministic/seasonal/break sensitivity and past-only forecast benchmarks before deciding on VECM or an alternative.
